bull.b: Sustained, industry‑leading margins indicate durable pricing power, efficient product mix, and high operating leverage. High margins support reinvestment in R&D, cushion against cyclical revenue swings, and enable sustained cash returns or strategic investments over the medium term.

Robust free cash flow and a very large cash balance provide flexibility to fund supply commitments, capex, M&A, and R&D without heavy leverage. High cash conversion supports capital allocation optionality and resilience through multi‑quarter customer or supply cycles.

bull.t: AI product momentum and platform innovation
bull.b: Clear adoption of Arista's AI fabrics and new hardware/software features represents a structural revenue driver. Platform wins, expanding customer base, and product innovations (e.g., liquid cooling) increase addressable market and create stickiness via integrated software and scale‑optimized solutions.

bear.t: Industry supply‑chain tightness and limited visibility
bear.b: Prolonged component constraints reduce the company's ability to fulfill demand predictably, forcing multiyear commitments and conservative booking. Limited visibility hampers customer planning and can elongate sales cycles or shift buyer timing, impacting revenue consistency over several quarters.

bear.t: Gross‑margin pressure from rising component costs
bear.b: Sustained upward pressure on memory and silicon costs and adverse product mix can compress margins even with strong pricing. If component cost inflation persists, profitability could decline versus historical peaks, reducing free cash flow and constraining margin‑dependent investments.

bear.t: Elevated working capital and large purchase commitments
bear.b: High inventory, elongated receivables and big multiyear chip commitments tie up cash and increase cash conversion volatility. This can pressure short‑term liquidity, elevate execution risk on supply agreements, and cause quarter‑to‑quarter earnings and cashflow variability despite strong long‑term demand.
